audit.why: Full and content charts agree row for row (Ziggs 1-3, Skill 4-5, Ziggs 6, Skill first item, Ziggs 2+) and the mirror proposed no side flips. The packet's only disagreement is level 6, which the prose already treats as her window while the chart calls it yours — worth a human look, but not worth breaking mirror agreement over a 6-game sample.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 and first-item spikes carry no cooldowns, and the first-item spike spends its whole length on an escape that does not work.
audit.why: The Hextech Ultimatum is 140/115/90s and only 475 range — it is a long-cooldown commitment you bait, not a constant threat. Hookshot is 16/15/14/13/12s and requires terrain. Tactical Sweep (W, 15s at rank 1) heals her off the outer half of the cone, so Grievous Wounds is the real first-item consideration.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text given the 140s R, spikes[2].text rebuilt on walls and anti-heal, dosFull[0].d given Hookshot's 16s and its terrain requirement.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three fields tell you to hold Satchel Charge to knock yourself out of her ultimate zone, and nothing mentions her true damage or her auto-reset opener.
audit.why: The Hextech Ultimatum anchors the target to the area — the point of the ability is that you cannot leave it, so a self-knockback repositions you inside the zone rather than out of it. Spending W that way loses your only disengage for 20s at rank 1. Precision Protocol (Q) is both an auto-attack reset and true damage on the empowered hit, so her burst opens on a wind-up and stacking resistances does not blunt it.
audit.corrected: wants.you[1], spikes[1].text, spikes[2].text and late no longer promise a Satchel escape from her R; whys[3] states the true damage; dontsFull[0].d carries the Precision Protocol reset tell.
